newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Moody's says may downgrade Atlas Copco.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says may downgrade Atlas Copco.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Moody's said on Monday it had put Swedish industrial engineer Atlas Copco under review for a possible downgrade.

Moody's said the rating action followed an announcement earlier Monday that Atlas Copco had entered into a seven billion crown or $900 million bid for Prime Service Inc, a U.S. equipment rental company.
Under the deal, Atlas Copco will acquire all of Prime Service's outstanding shares at $32 each and also assume Prime Service's debt for $260 million.

"The proposed acquisition appears to be a logical extension of Atlas Copco's existing business and could broaden the distribution base for its products, primarily in the compressor technique buiness area," Moody's said in a statement.
But Moody's said this was by far the largest acquisition that Atlas Copco has undertaken so far.

"Its all debt-financed bid will increase Atlas Copco's indebtedness very considerably - by some $1,160 million (including assumed debt) - and Moody's review will focus on assessing the company's ability to swiftly reduce debt to levels more consistent with the current rating," it said.
Atlas Copco currently has a Prime-1 short term rating.

Moody's said the review would further consider implications for Atlas Copco's overall strategy, the structure of the financing for this transaction and possible synergies from this vertical integration move.
Fellow credit rating agency, Standard & Poor's (S&P) also put Atlas Copco on creditwatch on Monday with negative implications.
Atlas Copco shares were trading 4.5 crowns higher at 214 crowns at 1305 GMT.
